To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the QTL for Fhb1, Qfhs.ifa-5A and Qfhs.ifi-6B are stable across different environments, and that QTL for resistance are located on all chromosomes except 7D.
the QTL Qfhs.ndsu-3B1, Qfhs.ndsus-3BS, Qfhs.ifa5, Qfhs.nf-3BS, and Qfhs.ndsum-5A are the most promising for marker assisted selection of FHB resistance.
QTL for FHR resistance are found in several mapping populations and on all chromosomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of molecular markers linked to QTL for FNB resistance and their use in wheat breeding.
the development of new wheat cultivars that combine high levels of resistance to FHB with other agronomically important traits.
the identification and utilization of QTL for FFB resistance in wheat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FHB resistance is a complex and polygenic trait, and no single QTL is sufficient for complete resistance.
QTL for F HB resistance are stable and useful in marker assisted breeding programmes.
QTL mapping studies have provided a wealth of information on the genetic basis of FHB resistance and the results have been used to improve FHB resistance of wheat cultivars in several countries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QTL identified in the different studies are useful for breeding programmes.
QTL for FHR resistance were found on 17 of 21 wheat chromosomes and that QTL for resistance against all FHB components were found.
FHB resistance QTL have been mapped in several independent studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
marker assisted breeding for FHB resistance is possible.
the FHB resistance genes are highly diverse in wheat.
the FHB resistance QTL identified in the past are not sufficient to develop wheat varieties with acceptable levels of FHB resistance.
